topPRs.title: ci: use short-lived GitHub App tokens via OIDC exchange
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Moves the GitHub write operations in CircleCI from long-lived tokens to short-lived GitHub App installation tokens, obtained by exchanging a CircleCI OIDC token at an STS endpoint (octo-sts).

- Adds a reusable `github-token-exchange` CircleCI command. It requests a CircleCI OIDC token for the configured audience, exchanges it for an installation token scoped to a named identity, and exports the result to later steps through `$BASH_ENV`. Only the HTTP status and the error message are printed, never a token. With `fail_on_error: false` the step warns and continues without setting the variable when the endpoint is not configured or the exchange fails.
- `daily-codegen` exchanges a token for the `superchain-registry-codegen` identity and uses it to push the `automated-codegen-*` branch and open the pull request. The commit identity now comes from `BOT_GIT_NAME` and `BOT_GIT_EMAIL`, and the step fails with a clear message if either is unset.
- `run-staging-report` exchanges a token for the `superchain-registry-staging-report` identity before running the report. If the exchange is unavailable, the job behaves as it does today.
- `print_staging_report` no longer looks up the authenticated user to find its previous comment, because installation tokens cannot call `GET /user`. The existing comment is found by the report marker already embedded in the comment body. Only comments that carry the marker and were written by a bot account, or by the login given by the new optional `--comment-author` flag (`GITHUB_COMMENT_AUTHOR`), are eligible. The most recent comment from the configured author is preferred, then the most recent one from a bot account. Marker comments from any other account are ignored, and a new comment is posted when none is eligible. Failing to post the comment still only logs a warning.

Environment variables the CI jobs now expect:

| Variable | Used by | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `STS_URL` | `github-token-exchange` | Base URL of the token exchange endpoint |
| `STS_AUDIENCE` | `github-token-exchange` | Audience requested for the CircleCI OIDC token |
| `BOT_GIT_NAME` | `daily-codegen` | Git author name for the automated commit |
| `BOT_GIT_EMAIL` | `daily-codegen` | Git author email for the automated commit |

`GITHUB_TOKEN_GOVERNANCE` is no longer read by any job.

topPRs.title: ci: run staging report on GitHub Actions
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Adds `.github/workflows/staging-report.yaml`, which runs `print_staging_report` on pull requests to `main` and posts the report with the workflow token (`contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`). The job is skipped for pull requests from forks, where secrets are not available.
- The workflow downloads the op-deployer binaries the report needs, uses no caches, and checks out without persisting credentials.
- `print_staging_report` no longer calls `GET /user` to find its previous comment. It looks for the report marker and only updates a comment written by the configured author (`--comment-author` / `GITHUB_COMMENT_AUTHOR`) or by a bot account. Comments written by people are never edited; if no eligible comment exists a new one is posted.
- Removes the `run-staging-report` job from the CircleCI `main` workflow. It is not a required status check.
- The workflow reads the `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL` and `MAINNET_RPC_URL` Actions secrets, which repository admins must provide before merge (same values CircleCI uses today).

topPRs.title: ci: move daily codegen to GitHub Actions with short-lived App tokens
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Adds `.github/workflows/codegen.yaml`, triggered daily at 15:00 UTC and by `workflow_dispatch`. It only runs on `main`.
- `generate` job (`contents: read`): checks out without persisting credentials, runs `ops/cmd/codegen` against the L1 RPC endpoints, and uploads `addresses.json`, `chainList.json` and `chainList.toml` as an artifact when they changed. No caches are used.
- `publish` job (`id-token: write` only, `codegen` environment): runs no repository code. It downloads the artifact, rejects anything outside the three expected files, enforces a size cap, checks that the JSON files parse, and compares blob SHAs with `main`. It then exchanges the workflow OIDC token for a short-lived GitHub App installation token via OIDC token exchange (octo-sts), creates an `automated-codegen-<timestamp>` branch, commits through the GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` mutation so the commit is signed by GitHub, and opens the pull request with the same title as before. The token is masked and revoked when the job exits.
- If `main` moved after the files were generated the run is skipped, and the next run picks the change up.
- Removes the CircleCI `daily-codegen` job, its long-lived token and its hardcoded git identity. `daily-check-review-period-delays` stays on the CircleCI schedule.
- The Slack messages the CircleCI job sent (new pull request, job failure) are not carried over.

topPRs.author: piohei
topPRs.body:
Update the public RPC, sequencer RPC, and explorer URLs for World Chain mainnet and Sepolia to use Worldcoin-managed endpoints. The RPC hosts proxy to Alchemy, and the explorer hosts redirect to the corresponding Alchemy explorers.

Updated the generated chain lists and ecosystem table. Verified that both public and sequencer RPCs return the expected chain IDs (480 and 4801), and that both explorer URLs return the expected redirects.
